title: Construction: reversible quadratic phases for the dirty stride solver (no new kappa)
body:
Extend [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) from constant site coefficients to the nonconstant quadratic
diagonal `D_j=exp(2 pi i a j^2/m)`. The leaf adds an approximation to
`(I-b D Z^w D^-1)^-1 x` to an arbitrary dirty target and restores the source
exactly. Its negative call reverses the complete grid word. The complete
factor interface keeps the original logarithmic borrowed-array count,
restores every borrowed array, and pays four phase passes around the whole
word. No phase array, cache, or free phase lookup is used.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9/research/dirty-stride-phases/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9/research/dirty-stride-phases/VALIDATION.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9/research/dirty-stride-phases/SOURCE.json).

The family includes the retained single-axis periodic chirp
`exp(-pi i s j^2/t)` for even `L=t`. For `L=8,a=-3,m=16,w=3`, the edge phases
have residues `11,9,7,5,3,1,15,13`; the ideal response differs from the
unphased response by more than `1/8` in a real component.

The implementation uses exact finite differences, a rounded Machin/Taylor
evaluator, three reversible real shears, and exact quarter-turns. The proof
bounds coefficient error and both directions of rounded conjugation,
including large dirty targets. Phase preparation costs `O((L+1)P)` scalar
steps with `P=W+O(log W)`. The full bill includes descriptors, input and
scratch storage, scalar widths, recurrence counters, data access, and tape
returns. This is a slower paid phase interface, with no fast-bit or runtime
speedup claim.

Reproduce with Python 3.11 or later and the standard library:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-stride-phases/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-stride-phases/test_package.py
```

The primary receipt checks 910 phase cases, 263 rounded leaves, 20 complete
factor words, two retained radix-four polynomial kernels, four larger tape
fixtures, and eight invalid-input controls. The kernel checks pay the exact
factor residual and execution error to a 128-bit total budget. All leaf
numerical cases have nonzero error; dirty data reaches `2^80`. Separate
full-angle rational intervals, geometric sums, and dense Gaussian elimination
supply the numerical oracles.

The package harness rejects 12 semantic, source, and type faults, then
regenerates the same receipt from a read-only relocated copy. Literal array
accesses are checked independently of the meter. Phase-shear intermediates
are measured; Machin integer widths use the stated analytical bound. Receipt
SHA256: `3305f81e9befe11133e85e0e38b5f0824c7a520d02e1799d5bf703e0bd1df740`.

Local isolated optimized checks pass on macOS arm64 / Python 3.14.7, as do
selected-record integrity and all 25 selected-result tests. The primary
replay took 65.20 seconds and the complete package harness 63.62 seconds;
these are verification durations. The scoped Python 3.11/3.14 workflow is
included; hosted CI and local Python 3.11 execution are separate. The full
repository suite and selected cold replay were not run for this isolated
addition. [VALIDATION.json](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9/research/dirty-stride-phases/VALIDATION.json) records the exact source freeze and limits.

Base: [8bddbee377e2f3ce1f1247196c4b290d55767d20](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/8bddbee377e2f3ce1f1247196c4b290d55767d20). [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) remains pinned at
[9df42a99dd8497b6e7d46cd2507bb89071372640](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/9df42a99dd8497b6e7d46cd2507bb89071372640), and [PR #479](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/479) at
`40dd01058439cdffae3e3b41c4fe52edaccf5f91`. The local derived solver has two
read-once validation edits because the pinned expressions each read twice
but charge once. The complete [DERIVATION.diff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9/research/dirty-stride-phases/DERIVATION.diff) is retained beside the
byte-exact original. No inverse arithmetic or transport instruction changes.
All 14 retained source files have SHA256 and Git-blob pins.

Credit Ali Romman (@aliromman)'s [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985), Rohan Guliani (@Rohansguliani)'s [PR #846](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/846), Charles Bethin (@cbethin)'s [PR #764](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/764),
Chafik Boukhalfa (@chafreaky)'s [PR #479](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/479) and [PR #628](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/628), Ross Richardson (@RossRichardson)'s [PR #948](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/948) for related
independent phase-state verification, and the retained manuscript lineage.
New material is prepared for Ali Romman (@aliromman), with substantial
OpenAI Codex assistance; original licenses and notices are retained.

No new kappa is claimed. The selected frontier and [upstream/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9/upstream) are unchanged.
This does not implement the multi-axis stream, arbitrary supplied phase
arrays, variable magnitudes, full transform, constant-coefficient precision
improvement, scalar bit-reversible compiler, physical supplier hosting, or
multiplication reduction. The finite checks support the written proof and
are not formal verification or independent human peer review.

Coordinator review: the proof, implementation and complete cost were read. A separate optimized package replay passed all 12 controls and reproduced the receipt from a read-only relocated copy.
